courses.title: Business and Technical Writing
courses.description: Study and practice of presenting technical information, with emphasis on formal and informal writing for the workplace, including resumes, job application letters, instructions, proposals, and reports.
courses.prerequisiteText: 010 core complete and 040 core complete

courses.title: Medical Writing
courses.description: The study and practice of interpreting and incorporating findings and statistical results into clear, comprehensible and well-organized prose.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: Proposal Writing
courses.description: Practice in writing and editing a series of proposals of varying scope and complexity.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: Environmental Writing
courses.description: Practice in presenting information about environmental issues as addressed by government, industry, private organizations and the mass media.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: Science Writing
courses.description: The study and practice of documenting, reporting and presenting science in articles, audiovisual scripts, specifications, reports and proposals.
courses.prerequisiteText: Prerequisite: 010 core complete and 040 core complete.

courses.title: General Biology I
courses.description: A survey of current biological concepts for students majoring in the sciences. Emphasis will be placed on biological molecules, cellular metabolism, cell division, heredity and the regulation of genes.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 1101, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete) and MATH 1301.

prerequisites.text: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 1101, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete) and MATH 1301.

courses.title: General Biology Laboratory I
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and experiments requiring scientific observation and analysis that illustrate some of the basic techniques, concepts and facts presented in BIOL 1301. (BIOL 1106)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 1301.

courses.title: General Biology II
courses.description: A survey of current biological concepts for students majoring in the sciences. Emphasis will be placed on topics which include evolution, biological diversity, ecology, and comparative structure and function of organ systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1101, BIOL 1301 and enrollment in BIOL 1102.

courses.title: General Biology Laboratory II
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and experiments requiring scientific observation and analysis that illustrate some of the basic techniques, concepts and facts presented in BIOL 1302. (BIOL 1107)
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1101 and credit or enrollment in BIOL 1302.

courses.title: General Chemistry I
courses.description: The first in a two course survey of the fundamentals of general chemistry for students majoring in the sciences. Descriptive material is correlated with the basic chemical principles and their applications. Modern concepts of atomic and molecular structure, chemical bonding, the gaseous state and the kinetic molecular theory of matter will be analyzed. There will be on stoichiometeric calculations of mass and molar relationships, energy relations and intermolecular forces.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1301 and CHEM 1107, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete), and one year of high school chemistry or CHEM 1305/CHEM 1105.

prerequisites.text: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1301 and CHEM 1107, ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete), and one year of high school chemistry or CHEM 1305/CHEM 1105.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory I
courses.description: Experiments which illustrate basic laboratory techniques and procedures, physical and chemical properties, stoichiometry, solutions, and thermochemistry. (CHEM 1111)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 1307.

courses.title: General Chemistry II
courses.description: The second in a two course survey of the fundamentals of general chemistry for students majoring in the sciences. Topics include liquids and solids, intermolecular forces, chemical kinetics, thermodynamics, homogeneous, heterogeneous and ionic equilibrium, modern concepts of acids and bases, electrochemistry, coordination chemistry, nuclear chemistry and selected topics.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in CHEM 1307 and credit or enrollment in CHEM 1108.

courses.title: General Chemistry Laboratory II
courses.description: Emphasis on reactions in aqueous solutions, gas laws, equilibrium, kinetics and qualitative analysis, with an introduction to instrumental analysis. (CHEM 1112)
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 1107 and credit or enrollment in CHEM 1308.

courses.title: Calculus I for the Natural Sciences
courses.description: Study of the concepts of differentiation and integration with an emphasis on applications in the life sciences. Topics include elementary functions and graphing, discrete models, discrete population models, limits, continuous functions, derivatives, differentiation with biological applications, linear approximation, optimization, difference equations, stability, and integration with biological applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better inMATH 1404 or MATH 1505 or placement by exam taken at UH-Downtown.

items.text: placement by exam taken at UH-Downtown

courses.title: Calculus I
courses.description: Functions, limits, the derivatives of algebraic and trigonometric functions, curve sketching, applications of the derivative, and an introduction to the definite and indefinite integrals of algebraic and trigonometric functions. (MATH 2413)
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MATH 1404 or in MATH 1505 or placement by exam taken at UH-Downtown.

items.text: placement by exam taken at UH-Downtown

courses.title: Calculus II for the Natural Sciences
courses.description: Topics include integration, approximation by Taylor series, differential equations, matrices, eigenvalues and eigenvectors, functions of several variables, partial derivatives, tangent planes and linearization, systems of difference equations, systems of linear and nonlinear differential equations, and equilibria and stability.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MATH 2411 or MATH 2401.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science with Visual Basic
courses.description: History, nature and uses of the computer; algorithms; number systems; information representation and organization with an overview of computer hardware and software, computing systems and major applications. An introduction to high-level languages and programming using Visual Basic with an emphasis on event-driven programming. Elements of the Visual Basic programming environment including objects, events, properties, user interface design and creating web-based applications are discussed. Practice with standard programming features such as control statements, subprograms, data types, arrays and input-output mechanisms.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1404 or MATH 1505 or MATH 1306; and placement in ENG 1301 or above.

courses.title: Introduction to Computer Science with Python
courses.description: This course introduces the fundamentals of computer programming using the Python language. The course is designed as an introductory course for students with or without prior programming experience. Topics include variable declaration, control statements, functions, I/O operations, exception handling, and data structures. The course provides extensive hands-on activities on writing computer programs.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1404 or MATH 1505.

courses.title: Statistical Analysis for Natural Science
courses.description: Basic concepts of statistics for natural science students are considered including collection of data, descriptive statistics, probability concepts, random variables, probability distributions, expected values, point and interval estimation techniques, hypothesis testing, bivariate data, linear regression, and analysis of variance. Natural science applications are stressed and computer statistical packages are used.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MATH 1404 or MATH 1505.

courses.title: General Microbiology
courses.description: An introduction to microorganisms (bacteria, viruses, yeasts, algae and protozoa) with attention to morphology, physiology, genetics, taxonomy, and relationship of microorganisms to soil, water, food, industry and health. Credit for both BIOL 1305 and 2305 may not be applied toward a degree. (BIOL 2321)
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102 and CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 and credit or enrollment in MBIO 2105.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102 and CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 and credit or enrollment in MBIO 2105.

courses.title: General Microbiology Lab
courses.description: Experiments which emphasize sterile technique, staining techniques, bacteria growth conditions, and biochemical tests used to identify microorganisms, phage testing, food microbiology, and Koch’s postulates. (BIOL 2121)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MBIO 2305.

courses.title: General Physics I
courses.description: This is the first in a two-part survey of general physics for science majors focusing on elementary principles of mechanics, heat and wave motion using elementary trigonometry and algebra. Topics include kinematics, dynamics of particles and rigid bodies; conservation of mass, momentum and energy; simple harmonic motion and characteristics of waves, mechanical and thermal properties of solids and fluids; and thermal properties, kinetics and dynamics of ideal gases. Credit for both PHYS 1307 and PHYS 2401 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MATH 1302 or the equivalent, enrollment in PHYS 1107.

courses.title: General Physics Laboratory I
courses.description: Topics include mechanics, bulk properties of matter, heat and waves. (PHYS 1101)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 1307.

courses.title: Physics I
courses.description: This is the first in a two-part survey of physics for science majors using calculus. Topics include kinematics and dynamics in one, two and three dimensions, statics, dynamics, potentials, conservation of energy and momentum (linear and angular), rotational kinematics and dynamics, oscillations, gravitation, fluid mechanics, thermal properties of matter, kinetic theory of gases and the first and second law of thermodynamics. Credit for both PHYS 1307 and PHYS 2401 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit in MATH 2402 (or MATH 2412) enrollment in PHYS 2101.

courses.title: Physics Laboratory I
courses.description: Topics include linear and rotational motion, collisions, simple harmonic motion and thermal properties of matter. (PHYS 2125)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 2401.

courses.title: General Physics II
courses.description: This is the second in a two-part survey of general physics for science majors focusing on elementary principles of electromagnetism, optics and modern physics using elementary trigonometry and algebra. Topics include static electric and magnetic fields and the motion of charged particles therein; induced electric and magnetic fields; DC and AC circuits; geometrical and physical optics; the concept of quantization and the properties of the atom and its nucleus. Credit for both PHYS 1308 and PHYS 2402 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: PHYS 1307 and credit or enrollment in PHYS 1108.

courses.title: General Physics Laboratory II
courses.description: Topics include electric and magnetic fields, DC and AC circuits, non-linear devices, geometric and physical optics, and atomic and molecular physics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 1308.

courses.title: Physics II
courses.description: This is the second in a two-part survey of physics for science majors using calculus. Topics include electric charge, electric fields and potentials, Gauss’ Law, capacitors and dielectrics, AC and DC electrical circuits, magnetic fields, the Biot-Savart Law, Faraday’s Law, magnetic properties of matter, Maxwell’s equations and electromagnetic waves and optics. Credit for both PHYS 1308 and PHYS 2402 may not be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Grade of C or better in PHYS 2401 and credit or enrollment in PHYS 2102.

courses.title: Physics Laboratory II
courses.description: Topics include static electric and magnetic fields and electron motion therein, DC and AC circuits including linear and nonlinear devices and properties of electromagnetic waves, and geometrical and physical optics. (PHYS 2126)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in PHYS 2402.

courses.title: General Genetics
courses.description: Fundamental principles of genetics including Mendelian inheritance, linkage, the chemical basis of genetics, mutations and chromosomal aberrations.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102,CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 2103.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102,CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 2103.

courses.title: General Genetics Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory topics designed to mimic classical genetic investigations. Experiments focus on the use of Drosophila melanogaster. Students conduct individual and group research projects.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 2303.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 2303.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I
courses.description: This course will cover various types of organic compounds, their classification, structure, naming, chemical and physical properties, reactivity, preparation, and techniques to identify them.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in CHEM 1308 and CHEM 1108. Enrollment in CHEM 2101 is recommended.

courses.title: Organic Chemistry I Laboratory
courses.description: Experiments illustrating basic techniques, synthesis, interpretation of spectra, use of molecular models and scientific literature.
courses.prerequisiteText: A letter grade of C or better in CHEM 2301 or enrollment in CHEM 2301.

courses.title: Biological Evolution
courses.description: Evolution is the central organizing paradigm in biology; aspects of biology can be understood without recourse to evolutionary theory but a deep understanding of biology and the diversity of life is impossible without it. This course seeks to establish a basic, solid understanding in what biological evolution is and its causes allowing the student to speak intelligently about evolution to others. Evidence of evolution, mechanisms for evolutionary change, adaptations, speciation, and phylogenetics are emphasized.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 2303.

courses.title: Biology Seminar
courses.description: Presentations and discussions related to recent research accomplishments in biology and biotechnology including student research presentations.
courses.prerequisiteText: Senior standing and majoring in an area of life science.

items.text: Majoring in an area of life science

courses.title: Microbiology Seminar
courses.description: Readings and student presentations of relevant articles from current scientific journals or the results of the research.
courses.prerequisiteText: MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105 and 8 hours of upper-level science.

prerequisites.text: MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105 and 8 hours of upper-level science.

courses.title: Seminar in Sustainability
courses.description: Presentations and discussions related to recent research accomplishments in the field of sustainability. Students will present scholarly research on sustainability efforts related to their major area of study. All students will summarize in writing and discuss orally the material presented by others so as to create cross-disciplinary expertise needed to solve complex problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: Senior standing.

prerequisites.text: Senior standing

courses.title: Undergraduate Research
courses.description: Independent investigation of a specific topic or problem in biology research under the direction of a selected faculty member.
courses.prerequisiteText: Approval by the Natural Sciences Department, minimum GPA of 2.0, and permission of instructor.

items.text: Approval by the Natural Sciences Department

courses.title: Wildlife Biology Laboratory
courses.description: Wildlife biology focuses on understanding wild animals and their habitats. Citizen science is a rapidly growing field involving the public generation of scientific knowledge. New opportunities for participating in citizen science are appearing constantly, and scientists need to understand how to tap into this valuable resource, especially as it applies to wildlife biology. In this course, students participate in an ongoing citizen science project, and design their own citizen science project related to wildlife biology. Students will also be trained in field techniques for observing local wildlife.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and 4 hours of biology above the 1000-level.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and 4 hours of biology above the 1000-level.

courses.title: Molecular Biology Laboratory
courses.description: Introduction to molecular biology techniques such as cloning genes and exploring their functions. Students will gain hands-on experience in gene cloning, PCR, plasmid construction, transformation, and functional assays. Laboratory work emphasizes carrying out student-designed experiments, problem solving, data analysis, and the presentation of scientific findings in written format.
courses.prerequisiteText: One of the following: BIOL 4320, BIOL 4330, CHEM 4140, MBIO 4310

courses.title: Cell Biology Laboratory
courses.description: This advanced laboratory course offers senior undergraduate students hands-on experience with research techniques in cell biology using mammalian cell lines. Students will engage in experimental design, data collection, analysis, and interpretation of results. Emphasis will be placed on student-driven experimental design, mastering laboratory techniques, and writing scientific reports.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 3103 or CHEM 4140

prerequisites.text: BIOL 3103 or CHEM 4140

courses.title: Environmental Laboratory and Field Studies
courses.description: The primary goal of this course is for students to gain experience in the design, execution, analysis, and communication of environmental field and laboratory studies. The first half of the semester includes weekly field trips to a variety of local ecosystems while the second half of the course is dedicated to student-designed projects.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 and 4 hours of biology above the 1000-level.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 and 4 hours of biology above the 1000-level.

courses.title: Senior Honors Thesis
courses.description: A research project, supervised by a member of the natural sciences faculty or a scientist at an affiliated research institution or laboratory. The completed research project must be presented in both written and oral form to the science faculty. No more than six hours credit for this course may be applied toward a degree.
courses.prerequisiteText: Senior standing and enrollment in the Honors Program in the Natural Sciences.

items.text: Enrollment in the Honors Program in the Natural Sciences

courses.title: General Ecology Laboratory
courses.description: Explore theoretical concepts and practical applications in ecology. Population dynamics will be investigated using computer simulations. Field sampling of local plant and animal populations will expose students to practical techniques of data collection and analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 3302.

courses.title: Developmental Biology Lab
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and experiments that illustrate some of the basic concepts, experimental techniques and facts presented in BIOL 3304.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 3304.

courses.title: Introduction to Neuroscience Lab
courses.description: This lab includes hands on experiments that focus on some basic principles of neuroscience including action potentials, structures and functions of neurons, with a focus on the connection between neuron networks and their behavior outputs. We will use Drosophila species as the model systems and introduce students to common approaches and techniques used in the field of neuroscience. These include immunohistochemistry, behavioral paradigms, and computational modeling. Students will then apply these techniques to explore research questions in a collaborative project.
courses.prerequisiteText: Enrollment or credit in BIOL 3307

courses.title: Histology Laboratory
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and experiments that illustrate some of the basic techniques, concepts and facts presented in BIOL 4310.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 4310.

courses.title: Cancer Biology
courses.description: A study of the molecular and cellular mechanisms of cancer including cell cycle regulation, genomic instability, cellular structural and metabolic changes, aberrant cell signaling and the cancer stem cell hypothesis. Drug development, drug resistance, and ethical considerations in cancer research and treatment will be discussed.
courses.prerequisiteText: General Genetics and laboratory (BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103)

courses.title: Cellular Biology
courses.description: The composition, structure, functions and dynamics of cells. Topics include interrelations of organelles, molecular transport and membrane trafficking, cytoskeletal interactions, nucleocytoplasmic relationships, intra- and intercellular communications, mechanisms of cellular death and laboratory analysis.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 2303and 6 hours of upper-level biology; credit for CHEM 2301 is recommended but not required.

courses.title: Molecular Biology
courses.description: Introduction to the molecular aspects of gene regulation in eukaryotic cells. Eukaryotic gene regulation is explored in the context of cell cycle regulation, cell differentiation, and cancer. The course emphasizes study of the primary research literature and the creation and testing of hypotheses using current technology.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit for BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and senior standing; credit for CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101 is recommended but not required.

prerequisites.text: Credit for BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and senior standing; credit for CHEM 2301/CHEM 2101 is recommended but not required.

courses.title: Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology
courses.description:
Crosslisted: CHEM 4344. Credit may only be earned for one.
Introduction to fundamental principles in pharmacology and toxicology. This course will highlight common molecular mechanisms of drug/toxin action, provide an ethical perspective on controlled research and experimental design, and provide students entering the chemical or medical industries an appreciation of modern drug design, industrial applications, clinical trials, and regulations imposed on the chemical industry to control public and private exposures.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 4340.

courses.title: Principles of Pharmacology and Toxicology
courses.description:
Crosslisted: BIOL 4344. Credit may only be earned for one.
This course will highlight common molecular mechanisms of drug/toxin action, provide an ethical perspective on controlled research and experimental design, and provide students entering the chemical or medical industries an appreciation of modern drug design, industrial applications, clinical trials, and regulations imposed on the chemical industry to control public and private exposures.
courses.prerequisiteText: CHEM 4340. Introduction to fundamental principles in pharmacology and toxicology.

courses.title: General Biochemistry Lab I
courses.description: Experiments in biochemistry to accompany CHEM 4340.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in CHEM 4340.

courses.title: General Biochemistry I
courses.description: Overview of fundamental biochemical principles, topics, techniques and analytical methods that integrates concepts from previous biology and chemistry courses to the study of biological macromolecules. Emphasis is placed on the bioorganic chemistry and techniques needed to critically and objectively analyze biological molecules and the fundamental processes that support life. Specifically protein, lipid and membrane structure and function, enzymatic catalysis and kinetics are emphasized.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1102 and BIOL 1302 and CHEM 2101 and CHEM 2301.

courses.title: Special Topics in Microbiology
courses.description: Selected topics in junior-level microbiology according to the needs and interests of the students.

prerequisites.text: No prerequisite statement published; review required.

courses.title: Immunology
courses.description: Innate immune response including latest advances, and detailed study of the adaptive immune response including B and T cell biology, macrophages, complement, hypersensitivities, transplantation and tumor biology.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105, BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103, and credit or concurrent enrollment in MBIO 4120.

prerequisites.text: A grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105, BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103, and credit or concurrent enrollment in MBIO 4120.

courses.title: Immunology Lab
courses.description: Introduction to immunology laboratory techniques including agglutination, precipitation, neutralization and labeled immunoassays.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MBIO 4320.

courses.title: Microbial Genetics
courses.description: This course will introduce the students to the field of bacterial molecular genetics, focusing on the mechanisms that bacteria have developed to evolve and adapt to changing environments. The molecular mechanisms of mutagenesis and gene transfer, along with the elements involved in these processes (plasmids, phages, transposons) and their regulation will be studied. These foundation concepts are needed to apply genetic approaches to explore microbial and evolutionary higher biological systems.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103, MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103, MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105.

courses.description: In-depth study of different topics in Microbiology and Immunology

courses.title: Plant Biology
courses.description: Comprehensive analysis regarding the biology of plants, including plant taxonomy, morphology, anatomy, physiology, reproduction, development, ecology, ethno botany and biotechnology.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 3130.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 3130.

courses.title: Plant Biology Laboratory
courses.description: Laboratory investigations and experimental analysis regarding the biology of plants, including plant taxonomy, morphology, anatomy, reproductive biology, nutrient requirements, photobiology, hormonal regulation, ecology, plant tissue culture and applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 3330.

courses.title: Plant Identification
courses.description: A study of the principles of naming, identification and classification of plants with an emphasis on the characteristics of select families of flowering plants.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102 and credit or enrollment in BIOL 3110.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102 and credit or enrollment in BIOL 3110.

courses.title: Plant Identification Laboratory
courses.description: Emphasizes plant identification and naming of plants from selected families of plants. A collection of local native plants will be required with appropriate scientific naming including family, genus, and species.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 3310.

courses.title: Biology of Fungi
courses.description:
Crosslisted: MBIO 3350. Credit may not be earned for both.
A comprehensive study of fungi with emphasis on the Kingdom Fungi, but consideration of various other organisms with a fungal lifestyle. Topics include classification, phylogeny and diversity, asexual and sexual characteristics and life cycles, growth, sporulation, nutrition, physiology and metabolism, genetics, ecology, symbiotic and pathogenic relationships, medical mycology, and biotechnology.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 or credit or enrollment in BIOL 3140.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 or credit or enrollment in BIOL 3140.

courses.title: Biology of Fungi Laboratory
courses.description:
Crosslisted: MBIO 3150. Credit may not be earned for both.
A study of the principles and applications of techniques for isolation, culture, and identification of fungi; and a study of the characteristics of fungal growth, nutrition, metabolism and genetics.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 3340.

courses.title: General Ecology
courses.description: The major goals of this course are for students to master the fundamental principles of organismal ecology, population ecology, community ecology, and ecosystem ecology. Students will apply these concepts to evaluate current and predict future ecological responses to global environmental changes.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 and enrollment or credit in BIOL 3102.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108 and enrollment or credit in BIOL 3102.

courses.title: Environmental Biology
courses.description: Ecological principles and current topics regarding the interrelationships among organisms and their environments, including analysis of human activities that impact natural ecosystems and cause environmental problems.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and 4 hours of biology above the 1000-level.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and 4 hours of biology above the 1000-level.

courses.title: Animal Behavior
courses.description: Behavioral capacities of the animal kingdom, with emphasis on methods of study, instinctive behavior, the biological basis of behavior, learning and intelligence and social behavior.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102 and ENG 1302.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102 and ENG 1302.

courses.title: Social Biology
courses.description: This discussion-format course is intended to bring together ideas and students from the disciplines of biology, psychology, sociology and anthropology. Its focus is on the area of animal behavior that involves the interaction of conspecifics. Topics to be discussed include aggression, courtship, parental behavior, altruism, behavior genetics, dominance, competition and cooperation, and behavioral ecology.
courses.prerequisiteText: 8 hours of biology, ENG 1302, PSY 1303 or SOC 1303, and junior standing.

courses.title: Environmental Microbiology
courses.description: The course will emphasize the impact of microorganisms on their environment. Topics include microbial diversity, microbiological interactions important in agriculture, medicine and biotechnology, biodegradation and bioremediation, and the impact of microbes in protective biofilms. Current methods for the detection of microorganisms and contamination control will also be discussed.
courses.prerequisiteText: Grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105.

prerequisites.text: Grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105.

courses.title: Human Anatomy Laboratory
courses.description: Appropriate exercises and activities that illustrate the techniques, concepts, and facts presented in BIOL 3305.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 3305.

courses.title: Developmental Biology
courses.description: A study of the mechanisms involved in growth and development of complex organisms. Topics include the molecular and cellular mechanisms of development and the genetics and early development of select invertebrate and vertebrate model systems. Additional emphasis will be placed on evolutionary developmental biology as well as on the connection between mechanisms of normal developmental and disease etiology.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and credit or enrollment in BIOL 3104.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and credit or enrollment in BIOL 3104.

courses.title: Human Anatomy
courses.description: A study of the structure of the human body using a systems approach. System and structural interactions will be examined. Structural and functional relationships will also be assessed.
courses.prerequisiteText: 8 hours of biology,CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and enrollment in BIOL 3105.

prerequisites.text: 8 hours of biology,CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and enrollment in BIOL 3105.

courses.title: Introduction to Neuroscience
courses.description: Introduction to Neuroscience is a lecture-based course designed to give an overview of the nervous system; including molecules, cells, development, circuits, and behaviors. These topics will be presented with respect to relevant biomedical research techniques and human pathologies/behaviors.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102; CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108; enrollment or credit in BIOL 3107.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102; CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108; enrollment or credit in BIOL 3107.

courses.title: Human Physiology
courses.description: A study of the function of the human body using a systems approach. Course will focus on the interaction of body systems and the maintenance of homeostasis. Some study of major disease processes associated with each system will be included.
courses.prerequisiteText: 8 hours of biology, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108.

courses.title: Human Genetics
courses.description: A study of inherited traits in humans with emphasis on the mapping of the human genome, molecular mechanisms of disease, karyotyping and chromosomal abnormalities, genetic testing, gene therapy, and ethical issues associated with human genetics.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103.

courses.title: Histology
courses.description: A comprehensive overview of the microscopic and submicroscopic anatomy of the vertebrate body, with emphasis on humans. Special topics include histochemistry, tissue culture and pathophysiology.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 4110.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 4110.

courses.title: Parasitology
courses.description:
Crosslisted: MBIO 4313. Credit may not be earned for both.
Introduction to parasitism as a biological concept and a survey of specific parasites of medical and veterinary importance. Additional topics include the relationship of opportunistic parasites in the treatment of AIDS, immunodiagnosis and the status of vaccine development for parasitic diseases.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 4113.

prerequisites.text: BIOL 1302/BIOL 1102, CHEM 1308/CHEM 1108, and credit or enrollment in BIOL 4113.

courses.title: Parasitology Laboratory
courses.description:
Crosslisted: MBIO 4113. Credit may not be earned for both.
Appropriate exercises and experiments that illustrate some of the basic techniques, concepts and facts presented in BIOL 4313.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in BIOL 4313.

courses.title: Physiological Ecology of Vertebrates
courses.description: Focus on mechanisms used by vertebrates to adapt to their natural habitats. Topics include the relationship between evolution and adaptation, nature and levels of adaptation, mechanisms of adaptation and the major adaptations of selected vertebrates. Emphasis on adaptation to extreme environments.
courses.prerequisiteText: BIOL 1302 and CHEM 2301.

courses.title: Virology
courses.description: The various groups of viruses are studied with regard to their structure, characteristics, mechanisms of replication, applications to molecular biology and to disease processes.
courses.prerequisiteText: MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105.

prerequisites.text: MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105.

courses.title: Medical Microbiology
courses.description: Microbial pathogens, clinical characterization, disease symptoms, mechanisms of pathogenesis, and chemotherapy.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105, BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and credit or enrollment in MBIO 4140.

prerequisites.text: A grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105, BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and credit or enrollment in MBIO 4140.

courses.title: Medical Microbiology Lab
courses.description: Techniques commonly used to identify clinically important pathogens and antibiotic testing.
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in MBIO 4340.

courses.title: Composition II
courses.description: English 1302 will build on the skills developed in ENG 1301 by focusing on research and analytical skills. Emphasis will be placed on the analysis and summarization of complex written, oral, and visual texts and the need to accurately paraphrase, quote and document sources through the development of college-level research skills.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in ENG 1301 or placement by examination.

courses.title: Introduction to Psychology
courses.description: A survey of the essential subject areas, major theories and approaches to the scientific study of behavior and mental processes. (PSYC 2301)
courses.prerequisiteText: Credit or enrollment in ENG 1301 (or 010 core complete)

courses.title: Introduction to Sociology
courses.description: An introduction to the scientific study of human society. This sociological perspective focuses on new ways of looking at society and its component parts, so the student is encouraged to develop a critical view of society, social processes and individual roles.

prerequisites.text: No prerequisite statement published; review required.

courses.title: Microbial Biotechnology
courses.description: Fundamental principles of biotechnology with emphasis on microbial systems, genetic improvement, and practical applications.
courses.prerequisiteText: A grade of C or better in MBIO 2305/MBIO 2105, BIOL 2303/BIOL 2103 and 8 additional hours of upper-level science.
